premises: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films/nanoribbons contain high internal stresses and defect densities that broaden the magnetocaloric response and increase hysteresis.
Annealing at 300–500°C relieves internal stresses and reduces defect density in similar alloy systems.
Reducing defect density decreases pinning of magnetic domain walls.
Decreased domain wall pinning narrows the magnetocaloric temperature window and reduces hysteresis.
